claims.text: Đơn Hàng's API serves a single shop through stage-3: the orders table has customer_id and no shop column; this module's multi-shop layouts run on separate lab databases (donhang_tenancy, donhang_shop_1/2), and the choice for Đơn Hàng is left to stage 4.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 and stage-3: STAGE.md, DonHang.Infrastructure/Migrations; DECISIONS.md §3 (2026-10-06, /outline backend multitenancy-and-sharding)

claims.text: OrdersController.List (lines 104-115 @ stage-2) gets the customer from CurrentCustomerAsync, which reads the token's sub (line 122) and looks it up via FindByIdentitySubjectAsync; line 113 passes that customer's id to ListByCustomerAsync, which returns only that customer's orders.

OrdersController.Create takes the customer from the token's sub via CurrentCustomerAsync, not from the request body (comment lines 22-24 @ stage-2); a caller with no customer row, such as a staff member, gets 403 (Forbid, line 111 in List) in Create and List.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 DonHang.Api/Controllers/OrdersController.cs lines 21-35, 104-115; ASP.NET Core docs: ControllerBase.Forbid with JWT bearer returns 403

claims.text: The access token's sub is signed by Keycloak and the API verifies the signature with Keycloak's public key, so a caller cannot change sub without the token failing validation.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: JwtBearer authentication, TokenValidationParameters (signature validation); lesson backend.l2.validating-provider-tokens

claims.text: OrderOwnerHandler @ stage-2 succeeds for any caller in the staff role (line 22) before comparing the caller's customer id with order.CustomerId; Get and Cancel ask for the OrderOwner policy, the check this handler implements, so any staff member can read and cancel any order.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 DonHang.Api/Authorization/OrderOwnerHandler.cs lines 16-35; OrdersController.cs Get, Cancel

claims.text: OrdersController.Ship (line 91 @ stage-2) uses [Authorize(Policy = "StaffOnly")], which lets in any caller with the staff role and checks nothing else, so any staff member can ship any order. OrdersController has five endpoints: Create, Get, Cancel, Ship, List.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2 DonHang.Api/Controllers/OrdersController.cs lines 86-97; Program.cs StaffOnly policy

claims.text: Request headers are chosen by the client; a server cannot trust a value in a header (such as a shop id) unless it is verified, e.g. carried in a signed token.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9110 §6.3 (header fields sent by the client); OWASP: do not trust client-supplied identifiers

claims.text: The tenant should be taken from the caller's verified identity (the validated token or a row found from it), never from a value in the request, when tenant isolation must hold against a dishonest caller.
claims.source_hint: OWASP: Broken Access Control / Insecure Direct Object Reference; same reasoning as OrdersController comment lines 22-23

claims.text: Tenants in one system share its CPU, database connections and limits set for all callers together (e.g. the stage-3 bulkhead limit on product reads), so one tenant's load can slow or refuse others' requests; limiting each request to its tenant's rows does not prevent this.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 DonHang.Api/Program.cs catalog-reads limiter; lesson backend.l3.bulkhead

claims.text: The stage-3 orders rate limit keeps one window per customer (sub) and applies only to OrdersController.Create ([EnableRateLimiting("orders")]), so it caps how many orders each customer places, not a shop with many customers.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3 DonHang.Api/Program.cs AddPolicy("orders") partition by sub; OrdersController.cs Create; lesson backend.l3.rate-limiting

claims.text: Running one copy of the application per shop means each copy is deployed, updated and monitored separately, so a fix ships once per shop; a multi-tenant system ships it once. Holds when copies are managed independently.
claims.source_hint: general operations reasoning; no single official source

claims.text: A query that omits the tenant filter does not fail; it returns rows of every tenant it matches.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: SELECT, WHERE clause (rows not filtered are returned)
